title: Allowlisting Client Connector in antivirus and host firewalls: paths, processes, firewall directions and the 100.64 range

prose.text: Endpoint protection can block Client Connector unless its binaries and processes are allowlisted. {{why-allowlist}}

prose.label: When a local firewall or antivirus error appears.
Open.
prose.text: How the 100.64 range is chosen when it changes, and where the active range shows, is open {{gap:cgnat-range-selection}}.

why-allowlist.statement: Zscaler recommends that users' devices have inbound rules that allow the Client Connector binaries and processes, and for some endpoint protection products such as antivirus and personal firewalls additional allowlists might need updating for full functionality. Because the app modifies the networking component of the operating system, Symantec Tamper Protection can trigger a false positive for the Zscaler service; the page says the warning can be ignored but the allowlist for Symantec Tamper Protection must be updated.

quotes: Zscaler recommends that your users' devices have inbound rules that allow the Zscaler Client Connector binaries and processes.
For some endpoint protection products like antivirus and personal firewalls, you might need to update additional allowlists for full Zscaler Client Connector functionality.
Because Zscaler Client Connector modifies the networking component of the operating system, a Symantec Tamper Protection can trigger a false positive for the Zscaler service.
While you can ignore this warning, you must update the allowlist for Symantec Tamper Protection.

windows-paths-by-bitness.statement: If an organization uses Group Policy Object (GPO) to push policies to both Windows 32-bit and 64-bit systems, the file paths of both versions must be in the GPO policy; the 32-bit files reside in the %ProgramFiles(x86) folder even on a 64-bit system, and Zscaler recommends migrating Windows 32-bit devices to 64-bit. Program files are typically on the C drive, with exceptions such as the D drive on Amazon WorkSpaces.

quotes: If your organization uses Group Policy Object (GPO) to push policies on both Windows 32-bit and Windows 64-bit systems, you must add the file paths of both versions to your GPO policy.
These files reside in the %ProgramFiles(x86) folder even if you are running the 32-bit version of Zscaler Client Connector on a 64-bit system.
To continue using the latest features, Zscaler recommends migrating Windows 32-bit devices to Windows 64-bit.
Typically, program files are located on the C drive. However, there are exceptions. For example, on Amazon WorkSpaces, program files are on the D drive.

cgnat-range.statement: With a GPO-managed or AV-managed host firewall, firewall rules can be configured for ZSATunnel.exe processes for all ports, protocols, network interfaces and network addresses. Client Connector also uses the carrier-grade NAT range 100.64.0.0/16 for internal health checking and for the Private Access service; if Zscaler sees a conflicting IP address it changes the range (for example to 100.65.0.0/16), anywhere from 100.64.0.0/16 to 100.83.0.0/16.

quotes: If you have a GPO-managed or AV-managed host firewall, you can configure firewall rules on your endpoint protection product for ZSATunnel.exe processes for all ports, protocols, network interfaces, and network addresses (e.g., 0.0.0.0/0).
Zscaler Client Connector also uses carrier-grade NAT range 100.64.0.0/16 as part of internal health checking and for the Private Access service.
For example, if you are using 100.64.0.0/16 and Zscaler sees a conflicting IP address, Zscaler changes it to 100.65.0.0/16.
This change in the IP addresses can range from 100.64.0.0/16 to 100.83.0.0/16.

windows-firewall-directions.statement: The Windows firewall bypasses listed are ZSATunnel.exe inbound and outbound, and outbound for ZSATray.exe, ZSATrayManager.exe, ZSAUpdater.exe, ZSAService.exe, Zscalerappupdater.exe, ZDPService.exe and ZEPInstaller.exe. Client Connector automatically adds required rules to Windows Defender Firewall, but if the Local Policy Merge GPO setting is enabled the rules are ignored and the firewall rules must be set up via the GPO; with Microsoft Defender Antivirus, any excluded paths and processes from the allowlist must be configured as custom exclusions.

Zscaler Client Connector automatically adds required firewall rules to the Windows Defender Firewall.
However, if the Local Policy Merge GPO setting is enabled, the rules are ignored and you must set up the firewall rules via the GPO.
If you use Microsoft Defender Antivirus, you must configure any excluded paths and excluded processes from the allowlist as custom exclusions.

macos-firewall.statement: On macOS, if machine tunnels are used with Transparent Proxy-based Interception mode enabled, inbound traffic to ZscalerTunnel must be allowed in firewall rules to allow access to Private Access apps, and FileVault must be disabled to allow Private Access connections before a user logs in. The macOS rules listed are Zscaler, ZscalerService and ZscalerUpdater outbound; ZscalerTunnel and UPMServiceController inbound and outbound; the autoupdate ZscalerUpdater inbound; and zdpd outbound.

quotes: If machine tunnels are used with Transparent Proxy-based Interception mode enabled, be sure to enable inbound traffic to ZscalerTunnel in your firewall rules to allow access to Private Access apps.
In addition, be sure to disable FileVault to allow Private Access connections before a user logs in to Zscaler Client Connector on their device.

linux-iptables.statement: Client Connector for Linux relies on the iptables command-line tool to configure the necessary rules within Netfilter. The vendor's commands, entered in the specified order, delete all rules, allow all outgoing connections, loopback connections, DHCP traffic, optionally SSH traffic, internal connections to the Client Connector adapter at 100.64.0.1, and established and related incoming connections, then deny everything else incoming.

quotes: The Zscaler Client Connector for Linux relies on the iptables command-line tool to configure the necessary rules within Netfilter.
You must enter the commands in the terminal window in the specified order:
Delete all rules: sudo iptables -F
Allow all outgoing connections: sudo iptables -I OUTPUT -j ACCEPT
Allow loopback connections: sudo iptables -A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT
Allow DHCP traffic:
Allow SSH traffic (optional, comment out if not needed):
Allow Zscaler Client Connector internal connections to the Zscaler Client Connector adapter: sudo iptables -I INPUT -d 100.64.0.1 -j ACCEPT
Allow established and related incoming connections: sudo iptables -A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
Deny everything else incoming: sudo iptables -A INPUT -j DROP

fw-av-error-check.statement: For a local FW/AV error after entering the rules, the vendor says to examine %windir%\system32\logfiles\firewall\pfirewall.log for drop entries for 100.64 addresses; drop entries mean the Windows Firewall rules are not applied correctly to allow Zscaler to communicate, and the rules must be revised based on the processes listed.

quotes: If you are receiving a local FW/AV error after entering the rules, examine the %windir%\system32\logfiles\firewall\pfirewall.log to verify that there are no drop entries for 100.64 addresses.
If you see drop entries, the Windows Firewall rules are not applied correctly to allow Zscaler to communicate.
You must revise the rules based on the processes listed earlier.

windows-processes.statement: Windows process roles per the article: ZSATray is the app UI; ZSATrayManager manages the tray process and checks signatures for communication between tray and system services; ZSATunnel handles traffic tunneling; ZSAService is the main service and the watchdog of all other services; ZSAUpdater monitors automatic updates; ZSAUpm is the Digital Experience (ZDX) service; zscalerchecksumverifier ensures the update being launched is legitimate; NetworkAdapter is the network adapter used in Tunnel (Route-Based); ProgramData\Zscaler stores logs, PCAPs and configuration; LogonUI is used for pre-Windows login in Private Access; ZDPService.exe evaluates DLP policy rules and determines the protection action; ZEPInstaller.exe prevents end users from stopping, modifying and deleting Zscaler products and services; ZSAMTAuthApp.exe supports authentication for the Machine Tunnel feature.

quotes: ZSATray: The UI of the Zscaler Client Connector application.
ZSATrayManager: Manages the tray process and checks signatures for communication between tray and system services.
ZSATunnel: Handles traffic tunneling.
ZSAService: The main service and the watchdog that looks after all other services.
ZSAUpdater: Monitors automatic updates for the Zscaler Client Connector application.
ZSAUpm: The Digital Experience (ZDX) service.
zscalerchecksumverifier: Ensures the update being launched is legitimate.
NetworkAdapter: Various versions of the network adapter that Zscaler Client Connector uses when in Tunnel (Route-Based).
ProgramData\Zscaler: Directory storing logs, PCAPs, and configuration for Zscaler Client Connector.
LogonUI: Used for pre-Windows login in Private Access.
ZDPService.exe: Evaluates Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy rules and determines the protection action to perform.
ZEPInstaller.exe: Prevents end users from stopping, modifying, and deleting Zscaler products and services.
ZSAMTAuthApp.exe: Supports authentication for the Machine Tunnel feature in Zscaler Client Connector.

macos-processes.statement: macOS process roles per the article: Zscaler provides the app interface; ZscalerService manages background service operations and communication between components; ZscalerTunnel handles network traffic tunneling; ZscalerUpdater manages software updates; UPMServiceController supports Digital Experience (ZDX) functionality; zdpd supports endpoint data protection functionality; com.zscaler.zscaler.TRPTunnel handles transparent proxy-based traffic interception.

quotes: Zscaler: Provides the Zscaler Client Connector application interface.
ZscalerService: Manages background service operations and communication between Zscaler Client Connector components.
ZscalerTunnel: Handles network traffic tunneling.
ZscalerUpdater: Manages Zscaler Client Connector software updates.
UPMServiceController: Supports Digital Experience (ZDX) functionality.
zdpd: Supports endpoint data protection functionality.
com.zscaler.zscaler.TRPTunnel: Handles transparent proxy-based traffic interception.

installed-footprint.statement: On Windows, installation creates the Zscaler-Network-Adapter folder and three services: ZSAService (a management service), ZSATunnel (a packet handling service that tunnels traffic to the Zscaler service) and ZSAUpdater (the update service). On macOS the Zscaler folder is in the list of applications, and on Linux the /opt/zscaler directory is created.

quotes: Zscaler-Network-Adapter
ZSAService: This is a management service for Zscaler Client Connector.
ZSATunnel: This is a packet handling service responsible for tunneling traffic to the Zscaler service.
ZSAUpdater: This is the Zscaler Client Connector Update service.
When Zscaler Client Connector is installed on users' macOS devices, you can find the Zscaler folder in their list of applications.
When Zscaler Client Connector is installed on users' Linux devices, the /opt/zscaler directory is created.

cgnat-range-selection.title: How the 100.64 range is chosen when it shifts, and where the active range can be seen
cgnat-range-selection.detail: The article says Zscaler changes the range on a conflict, between 100.64.0.0/16 and 100.83.0.0/16; it does not say how the new range is chosen or where the active one shows. It also gives no rules for nftables, firewalld or ufw beyond naming iptables.
